subject: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.

messages.author: eaf891916146cc5e
messages.subject: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.
parts:
Hi!


I computed four models with the raw data as input and the same 4 models with the covariance matrix as input. In the first three models, the SEM results are similar. Only in Model 4, I found similar good fit statistics, but different parameters estimates.


Here is the model:

m <- '# measurements model - bifactor: 2-factor model

    pr =~ b1*antisaccade + b2*stopsignal + b3*colorstroop + b4*simon + b5*long + b6*local

    di =~ b7*arrowflanker + b8*letterflanker + b9*numberstroop + b10*short

    inhib =~ b11*antisaccade + b12*stopsignal + b13*colorstroop + b14*simon + b15*long + b16*local + b17*arrowflanker + b18*letterflanker + b19*numberstroop + b20*short

    # constraints

    b1 > 0

    b2 > 0

    b3 > 0

    b4 > 0

    b5 > 0

    b6 > 0

    b7 > 0

    b8 > 0

    b14 > 0

    b16 > 0

    b18 > 0

    b19 > 0

    b20 > 0

    # regressions

    pr ~ age_group

    di ~ age_group

    inhib ~ age_group

    # (co) variances

    pr ~~ 0*di

    inhib ~~ 0*pr

    inhib ~~ 0*di'

 

I used the following code to compute the model:

## With raw data as input

fit.raw <- sem(m, data=d, std.lv = TRUE)

## With covariance matrix as input

fit.cov <- sem(m, sample.cov = cov.matrix, sample.nobs = sample_size, std.lv = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.
parts: Can someone see the reason why the results are different in Model 4?

Probably not without having your data.  Do you have missing data?  If so, perhaps you used listwise deletion (lavaan's default) with the raw data, but perhaps pairwise deletion when calculating the covariance matrix: cov(data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.
parts:
Compare the actual covariance matrices used: use

inspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov

for both methods; the should be identical.

Depending on how you have compute the covariance matrix, you may need to
set the argument sample.cov.rescale to FALSE (TRUE is the default, if
estimator = "ML")

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.
parts: No, I don`t have any missing data in this dataset. But thanks for the idea!

messages.author: eaf891916146cc5e
messages.subject: Re: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.
parts:
As suggested, I used "inspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov" for both computations. The covariance matrices are similar in both cases when I round to 4 decimal places. There are, however, small differences when I round to 20 decimal places. But could such small differences in the covariance matrices explain the large difference in the parameter estimates?
I also tried with sample.cov.rescale = FALSE. But this resulted in the same problem (i.e., large differences in the parameter estimates).

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Difference in SEM results when raw data or covariance matrix is used as input.
parts:
Something else must be going on. If the sample covariances are the same,
and all the other options are the same, the end result must be the same.
Could you wrap this up in a reproducible example?

Yves.
